text:
La Parima is the pharaonic dream

and Moses' stone,

the Sister's black honeycomb,

which Brother Francis did not come to know.

Cathedral of mystery, Southern Range, unknown,

hidden tongue of the voice of water,

God's badly closed eyelid, letting show

the blue thread of a glance.


I dreamed, for your Glory,

river of the Homeland,

of writing an essential word

on the sheet of the savanna,

wetting in your dark springs

the celestial sting of a heron's feather.

But I found only my blood,

its red thinned by the mixture of tears.


Yet I offered to come to you

and I am on your path!

You will emerge from your springs: the God of Parima,

the Indian God, will open the door for you

of his great dark house; the Old God

will let you come as he does every day,

and I will be on your path…

You emerge from the hands of your mountain,

as a miracle emerges from the hand of God,

as every night, from the cage of the sky,

the Bird of the Sun escapes and goes to the fields.

translation.title: La Parima and the Springs
translation.editorial_note: La Parima, the Southern Range, and the Indigenous/Old God imagery are retained; “Sister” and “Brother Francis” follow the source’s capitalized kinship terms.
